center.h2: Collecting Directory ACL Details - Powershell Script

ul.li: The MS Windows AD Objects application provides an embedded add-on with a simple Powershell script that can be leveraged for collecting the ACL, Size, File Count and Sub-Directory Count for a single or multiple Windows Directories. The data collected can then be correlated with the AD User/Group Lookups to enhance the ACL IDs. Also, if File Auditing is enabled, you can use the File Auditing Drilldown to review the Windows Events for the selected objects using native Windows File Object Auditing.

p.i: Components used for the ACL data collection Script:

li.i: This add-on is Not available on Splunkbase, it is embedded in the MS Windows AD Objects application's folders - ...\splunk\etc\apps\ms_windows_ad_objects\appserver\static\ex_win_ta\ms_ad_obj_ta_acl.zip

ul.li: Description: This zip file contains the content you can use for creating a TA to collect local or remote (via UNC Path) ACL Details for specified directories.

How to Use: This zip file contains the PowerShell script, example inputs.conf and supporting scripted input files. You can either use this app, or create a new TA and add the .conf/script files to it or add them to an existing TA already deployed to your Windows Splunk Forwarders.

bin/... files:
runpowershell.cmd
Description: This file is only used when the "Invoke-MonitoredScript" method is used. It is an optional PowerShell exe location pointer file, used when working with PowerShell versions below 3.0.
Deployed Example Location (Ex App: ms_ad_obj_ta_acl): C:\Program Files\SplunkUniversalForwarder\etc\apps\ms_ad_obj_ta_acl\bin\runpowershell.cmd
Invoke-MonitoredScript.ps1
Description: This file is only used when the "Invoke-MonitoredScript" method is used. This script is used to initiate the powershell script \powershell\splunk_win_acls.ps1.
Deployed Example Location (Ex App: ms_ad_obj_ta_acl): C:\Program Files\SplunkUniversalForwarder\etc\apps\ms_ad_obj_ta_acl\bin\Invoke-MonitoredScript.ps1

bin/powershell/... files:
splunk_win_acls.ps1
Description: This is the main powershell script that first retreives the target list of directories you enter in the text file (splunk_win_acls_list.txt). After getting the list of target directories, it then uses the Get Content PowerShell command to recursively retrieve the data for the sub-directories, and the Get-Acl Powershell Command to retrieve the current Access Control List (IdentityReference, FileSystemRights, AccessControlType, IsInherited, InheritanceFlags, and PropagationFlags) information.
Deployed Example Location (Ex App: ms_ad_obj_ta_acl): C:\Program Files\SplunkUniversalForwarder\etc\apps\ms_ad_obj_ta_acl\bin\powershell\splunk_win_acls.ps1
splunk_win_acls_list.txt
Description: This is a simple text file that contains 1 or more Local/UNC Path directies that you want to collect the ACL details from, including the sub-directories. If you want to specify multiple target directories, then enter each target directory on it's own line. If you are going to specify a UNC Path, then ensure that you have the Splunk Service running as an AD Account that has access to the remote directory.
Deployed Example Location (Ex App: ms_ad_obj_ta_acl): C:\Program Files\SplunkUniversalForwarder\etc\apps\ms_ad_obj_ta_acl\bin\powershell\splunk_win_acls_list.txt

div.h4: Steps for Deploying the ACL data collection Script (splunk_win_acls.ps1):

ol.li: Click to download ms_ad_obj_ta_acl.zip file locally

Extract the contents of the ms_ad_obj_ta_acl.zip file.
Note: The ms_ad_obj_ta_acl app is located in the extracted Windows Folder Acl TA folder.
Navigate into the ...\Windows Folder Acl TA\ms_ad_obj_ta_acl\bin\powershell\ directory.

Using a text editor, open the splunk_win_acls_list.txt file.
This file is used by the splunk_win_acls.ps1 powershell script to determine what folders, and subfolders, to retrieve the ACL data from.
First, replace the example directories and then Add any addittional Local or UNC Path locations for the target directories, subdirectories, you want to collect ACL Data for:
Example: C:\Critical_Files \\test_server\c$\Important_files
Save the Changes to the splunk_win_acls_list.txt file
Navigate into the ...\Windows Folder Acl TA\ms_ad_obj_ta_acl\local\ directory.

Using a text editor, open the inputs.conf file.
For the below input, update the setting(s), disabled from 1 to 0, and optionally the index if you have your Windows data going to a different index then windows index. You can also adjust the schedule setting. [powershell://splunk_win_acls] script = ."$SplunkHome\etc\apps\ms_ad_obj_ta_windows_acl\bin\powershell\splunk_win_acls.ps1" schedule = 0 */24 * * * sourcetype = WinDirAcl source = Powershell index=windows disabled = 1
Save the changes to the ...\Windows Folder Acl TA\ms_ad_obj_ta_acl\local\inputs.conf file.

Copy the (ms_ad_obj_ta_acl) folder, DO Not Copy the Windows Folder Acl TA parent folder, and paste the ms_ad_obj_ta_acl in either the (...\splunk\etc\deployment-apps\) directory if using Deployment Server or to a directory that the target remote system will have access to.

Either complete the Deployment Server steps for adding the the ms_ad_obj_ta_acl app to a server class. Or by manually copying to the ms_ad_obj_ta_acl folder into a remote Splunk Forwarder system's ...\splunkUniversalForwarder\etc\apps directory.

li.i: If you want to use a different name than ms_ad_obj_ta_acl, you will need to update the referenced paths in the inputs.conf, and ...\ms_ad_obj_ta_acl\bin\Invoke-MonitoredScript.ps1. with the new app folder name)

ul.li: Once the data is received you can see the results in this dashboard MS Windows AD Objects / Windows / File Auditing / AD Objects - File ACL - Analysis

div.i: Step 1: Deploy Security Auditing with Central Audit Policies
div.p: In this step, you configure the global object access policy on the domain controller.

li.p: Applies to (Windows 10, Windows Server 2016, Windows Server 2012 R2, Windows Server 2012)
You can apply audit policies to individual files and folders on your computer by setting the permission type to record successful access attempts or failed access attempts in the security log.
To complete this procedure, you must be signed in as a member of the built-in Administrators group or have Manage auditing and security log rights.

p.strong: In this step, you configure the global object access policy on the domain controller.

li.p: Sign in to the domain controller as an Administrator
In Server Manager, point to Tools, and then click Group Policy Management.
Navigate to the designated Group Policy that is associated with the Organization Unit/Container where the targeted "File Audit" Computer Accounts are located.
Right-Click on the Group Policy and Click Edit
Double-click Computer Configuration, double-click Policies, and then double-click Windows Settings.
Double-click Security Settings, double-click Advanced Audit Policy Configuration, and then double-click Audit Policies.
Double-click Object Access, and then double-click Audit File System.
Select the Configure the following events check box, select the Success and Failure check boxes, and then click OK.
In the navigation pane, double-click Global Object Access Auditing, and then double-click File system
In the navigation pane, double-click Global Object Access Auditing, and then double-click File system
In the Advanced Security Settings dialog box, select the Auditing tab, and then select Continue.
Select the Define this policy setting check box, and click Configure.
In the Advanced Security Settings for Global File SACL box, click Add, then click Select a principal, type Everyone (Or another group with users you want to specifically audit), and then click OK.
Optional: In the Add a condition: section, click Add a condition and in the drop-down lists select (Ex. [Resource] [Department] [Any of] [Value] [Finance] )
Click OK three times to complete the configuration of the global object access audit policy setting..

li.i: Complete the Steps in the Applying Auditing to file or folder: section below on the Target Computers and Folders you would like to audit.

div.i: Step 2: Applying Auditing to file or folder:

summary.i: How to Apply a basic audit policy on a file or folder

li.p: Before you set up auditing for files and folders, you must enable object access auditing. To do this, follow the steps above to define auditing policy settings for the object access event category. If you don't enable object access auditing, you'll receive an error message when you set up auditing for files and folders, and no files or folders will be audited.
Applies to (Windows 10, Windows Server 2016, Windows Server 2012 R2, Windows Server 2012)
You can apply audit policies to individual files and folders on your computer by setting the permission type to record successful access attempts or failed access attempts in the security log.
To complete this procedure, you must be signed in as a member of the built-in Administrators group or have Manage auditing and security log rights.

p.strong: To apply or modify auditing policy settings for a local file or folder

li.p: Select and hold (or right-click) the file or folder that you want to audit, select Properties, and then select the Security tab.
Select Advanced.
In the Advanced Security Settings dialog box, select the Auditing tab, and then select Continue.
Do one of the following:

ul.li: To set up auditing for a new user or group, select Add. Select Select a principal, type the name of the user or group that you want, and then select OK.
To remove auditing for an existing group or user, select the group or user name, select Remove, select OK, and then skip the rest of this procedure.
To view or change auditing for an existing group or user, select its name, and then select Edit.

li.p: In the Type box, indicate what actions you want to audit by selecting the appropriate check boxes:

ul.li: To audit successful events, select Success.
To audit failure events, select Fail.
To audit all events, select All.

li.p: In the Applies to box, select the object(s) to which the audit of events will apply. These include:
By default, the selected Basic Permissions to audit are the following:

ul.li:
Additionally, with your selected audit combination, you can select any combination of the following permissions:
Full control
Modify
Write
